---
internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

id: B_259
internalId: e461b100-4b8f-435e-9c0f-81426d7fdb47
title: Responsive search reopens after Escape and loses results on resize
status: new
---

Reported during review of [PR #27](https://github.com/jan-bogaerts/md2/pull/27), head `e1181650a`. Fix after the PR is merged.

## Search reopens after Escape

1. Use a window width where search shows the shortcut presentation.
2. Open search by clicking its launcher.
3. Press Escape.

The popover closes and immediately reopens. Closing should dismiss search and leave keyboard navigation usable.

`SearchControl` uses a MUI `Popover` that restores focus to the launcher on close. `SearchLauncher` opens search through its `onFocus` handler, so restored focus opens it again. A targeted regression probe reproduced the failure; disabling focus restoration in a temporary probe prevented reopening.

Affected files: `app/src/components/shell/search/search_control.tsx` and `search_launcher.tsx`.

## Resizing clears results and search options

1. Open inline search and enter a query that returns a result, such as `Beta` in the existing test fixture.
2. Resize until search changes to a popover presentation.

The query remains, but the matching results disappear. RegExp mode and the background-body/action options also reset. Resizing should preserve the active search, its options, and matching results in either direction.

`SearchControl` mounts `SearchPanel` in separate inline and popover branches. Changing presentation remounts the panel. Only the query survives in `SearchControl`; `SearchPanel` initializes empty results and default options and does not apply its initial query on mount.

Affected files: `app/src/components/shell/search/search_control.tsx` and `search_panel.tsx`.

## Regression coverage

- Open shortcut search, press Escape, and verify it stays closed without preventing later reopening.
- Search for a matching card and resize between inline and popover presentations; verify the query and result remain available.
- Enable RegExp mode and background-body/action options before resizing; verify their selections and search behavior survive.

Both reported failures were reproduced with temporary probes in `search_control.test.tsx`; the probes were removed after review. No fix is included in this report.

---
id: B_264
internalId: 78b279d6-eae4-4801-92c0-a6423a1fc880
title: Action input rerenders unrelated controls while typing
status: new
---

## Problem and evidence

With one action popup open and no action running, typing repeatedly renders unrelated popup controls and the Markdown editor wrapper/plugin tree. This violates the [architecture rule](../architecture/architectural_decisions.md) that layout components compose regions and subscriptions belong at the smallest boundary rendering the changing value.

The [performance trace](file:///C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/Trace-type-action-input.json) investigated for [F_411](F_411_action_input_does_mysterious_things.md) contains 429 React render markers and 225 commit markers between 6.34 and 40.46 seconds, with 137 input events. Repeated component records include `ActionPopupBottomRow`, `ActionAgentSelectors`, `ActionPromptMenu`, `ActionAgentPrompt`, `MarkdownEditor`, and editor plugins. These aggregate development-mode records are not one-to-one counts of keystrokes or visible changes.

This bug concerns excessive rendering. The trace does not establish the cause of the separately reported chatlog flicker.

## Verified causes and affected code

- `action_popup_bottom_row.tsx` subscribes to the complete prompt string. Every published draft edit renders the footer, including agent/model/security selectors and the prompt menu. Its displayed prompt-dependent decisions use whether trimmed text is empty, rather than the actual text.
- `action_agent_prompt.tsx` also subscribes to the complete prompt string, but uses it only to derive `promptEmpty`. Its rerender recreates `handleLiveChange` and processes the editor subtree even when emptiness and layout have not changed.
- `MarkdownDraft.edit()` publishes `valueChanged` when text changes. `ActionPromptDraft` forwards that subscription. The editor already has a separate external-replacement subscription through `useMarkdownDraft`; ordinary editor input must not cause an external replacement or remount.

Affected boundaries: the two components above, `ActionAgentSelectors`, `ActionPromptMenu`, `ActionPromptDraft`, and the draft/editor binding. Inspect editor plugin subscriptions separately before attributing their own selection or content updates to this parent-render problem.

## Required behavior

entries.content:
**Yes: while the popup remains mounted, a successful catalog load starts another five-minute countdown, which triggers another automatic refresh.** It repeats without any model-list change. A failed refresh stops that automatic cycle.

The implementation has departed from the manually configured model-list design.

**What changed**

Commit `464158ce0` (“discover provider models and support OpenAI Fast mode”, October 3) introduced runtime discovery:

- **Codex:** starts a separate `codex app-server --stdio` process and requests models, provider configuration, and Fast-mode policy.
- **Claude:** starts a separate Claude process and reads the models returned during initialization.
- **Other agents:** constructs the catalog from the manually configured `profile.models`.

The [discovery switch](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/shared/agent_profiles.mjs:262) selects runtime discovery solely by the names `codex` and `claude`. Their configured model lists are therefore no longer the source for these selectors.

That conflicts with the existing [action-editor description](</C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/design/architecture/initial description/writings/action_editor.md:74>): “Each configured agent profile owns its available model list.”

**Where the catalog is used**

| Consumer | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Action popup settings | Model choices, thinking levels, Fast availability, selection validation |
| Popup run controls and shortcuts | Catalog state becomes a reason to disable execution |
| Popup message | Displays “Refreshing model capabilities” |
| Action-definition editor | Model, thinking-level, and speed choices |
| Configuration editor | Default model settings and manual refresh |
| Application agent menu | Model/settings choices and manual refresh |
| Backend action execution | Validates selected capabilities and builds execution arguments |
| Agent-assisted search | Uses the same backend execution resolution |

Within the popup, `useActionRunSettings` is consumed by **six components**: selectors, footer, prompt owner, disabled-message display, preset name, and response-prompt buttons. They share cached requests, but all inherit the catalog’s loading/error/stale state.

**Why it is complex**

It was implemented as **runtime capability discovery**, including provider-specific reasoning and Fast-mode capabilities, rather than reading a configured list. Consequently, it adds:

- Two caches: renderer and Electron backend.
- Cache contexts for profile, connection, project/worktree, executable, environment, and configuration-file fingerprints.
- Discovery subprocesses, concurrent-request deduplication, probe limits, cache eviction, and stale-result checks.
- Loading/error/stale state propagated into UI and execution validation.

Those mechanisms explain the complexity; they do not justify it for your stated requirement.

**Why five minutes**

There are two independent five-minute policies:

1. The [renderer service](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/agents/agent_capabilities_service.ts:181) actively marks a catalog stale. The mounted hook responds by requesting a forced refresh—even for catalogs constructed from manually configured profiles.
2. The [backend service](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_model_catalog_service.js:87) rejects cached discovery results older than five minutes when another request arrives. It has no recurring refresh timer itself.

**I found no documented reason for choosing five minutes.** Neither policy requires evidence that models changed. The timer treats elapsed time as a change, and the popup incorrectly turns that artificial staleness into a message and execution blocker.

For the manually maintained list you describe, this timing machinery has no purpose. No files changed.

* the processes that are stared to discover the models, do they remain open or is it a one-shot get values?
* are these model-discovery processes triggered through the manual 'refresh models' button or are they started automatically with a timer
* why do we have a timer at all when the refresh needs to be done manually
I’ll check the discovery-process cleanup and every refresh trigger to answer those three points precisely.

1. **They are one-shot discovery processes.** They start, retrieve the catalog, then the service terminates their process tree in a `finally` block—on success or failure. They are not retained between refreshes. A separate **20-second timeout** bounds discovery; that timeout serves a valid cleanup purpose. See [process lifecycle](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_model_catalog_service.js:100).

2. **Both manual and automatic triggers start them:**
   - Clicking **Refresh models** forces discovery.
   - Mounting a catalog consumer automatically loads it when missing.
   - Five-minute expiry triggers automatic discovery while a consumer remains mounted.
   - Starting an action or agent-assisted search can trigger discovery if the backend cache is expired or its inputs changed.

   Custom agents using configured model lists do not start discovery processes.

3. **There is no justification for the five-minute refresh timer under your manual-refresh requirement.** The implementation assumes catalogs should automatically stay “fresh”; it does not detect an actual model-list update. Every successful automatic refresh restarts that countdown.

   There are two expiry mechanisms to address: the **renderer timer** and the **backend’s five-minute cache-age check**. Removing only the renderer timer would still allow execution to trigger discovery after cache expiry.

The manual-refresh button is therefore currently an additional trigger, not the exclusive trigger. That is the implementation mismatch.

* remove everything related to the timer refresh
* why is the backend caching anything here, why does the backend know about the models at all? this seems wrong, it gets the name of the model it should use, that is it

I’ll remove the automatic expiry and refresh cycle while preserving initial loading and the manual “Refresh models” action. I’ll also trace why execution consults the backend catalog and explain that separately; I won’t change that behavior without your instruction.

internalId: 583d9c88-b71c-4560-92ad-3e23d33bf1d0
---

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. Do not hoist changing data into ancestors only to pass it downward. | Limits rerenders to affected UI, protects transient state such as open popups, and avoids broad prop chains. |
| Components use the app theme service path. | `App` owns theme mode through `useThemeMode()`, builds the MUI theme with `createAppTheme(mode)`, and provides it through `ThemeProvider`. Components read theme values with MUI APIs such as `useTheme`, `useMediaQuery`, and `sx`; only controls that change the palette mode receive `mode` and `onToggleTheme`. | Theme state, persistence, and palette construction stay centralized while components remain presentation-focused. |

When those change, a normal read returns configured models, while the frontend retains its discovered catalog. I reproduced execution rejecting a previously discovered model that the UI still considers valid. Preserve discovered catalogs until startup or manual refresh replaces them.

2. **[P2] Failed refresh deletes the usable desktop catalog.** [Manual refresh deletes the cache before discovery succeeds](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_model_catalog_service.js:84), but the [frontend retains the previous catalog](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/agents/agent_capabilities_service.ts:183). Send remains enabled, yet execution can reject that model or its Fast setting. I reproduced this. Replace the cached catalog only after successful discovery.

The periodic timers and expiry callbacks are removed. I found no dead code from that mechanism; `stale` still serves refresh and failure states.

Both linters passed, and 32 focused tests passed. Broader component tests were blocked during import by `EMFILE: too many open files`, including on retry with lower concurrency.

No files changed.
Fingerprint? where does this word come from. I don't understand what you are saying. use normal english

“Fingerprint” is the code’s name for checking whether the agent program or its configuration files have changed. I should have explained that plainly.

The two problems are:

1. If those files change, the backend stops using the model list it discovered earlier. The interface still shows that list, so you can select a model and then have Send fail.
2. If a manual refresh fails, the backend has already deleted its previous model list. The interface keeps showing it, which can cause the same failure.

Both problems come from the interface and backend using different model lists.
wtf? are we really comparing files here?

Yes. Each backend model-list read checks file sizes and modification times for the agent program and several configuration files, including Codex’s model cache. It doesn’t compare file contents.

That checking was already there before this change. Removing periodic refreshes left it in place, so a file change can still make the backend stop using its previously discovered model list.
and why are we doing this?

It was there to avoid reusing an outdated model list after an agent update or a configuration change—for example, switching providers or accounts.

With the new rule—refresh only at startup or manually—that automatic invalidation no longer fits. It remained in the implementation, and now discards the cached list without discovering a replacement. That’s the leftover behavior I flagged.
remove the entire 'fingerprint' operation. this is completely over engineered
I’ll remove the file checks and use the agent profile and working directory to identify cached model lists. I’ll update the affected tests and run the desktop checks.
